title.en: RMS and Average Values Explained Simply

narration.en: Concept video: Reactance of L and C Explained Simply

body.en: In series, the resistor voltage is in phase with the current while the reactive voltages are at 90°, so they add as vectors (phasors). The total opposition is the impedance $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$ and $I = V/Z$. The *phase angle* is given by $\tan φ = (X_L - X_C)/R$. If $X_L > X_C$ the circuit is inductive (current lags); if $X_C > X_L$ it is capacitive (current leads).
body.kn: ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ರೋಧಕ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ಪ್ರವಾಹದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪ್ರತಿಘಾತ ವಿಭವಾಂತರಗಳು 90° ನಲ್ಲಿ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಅವು ಸದಿಶಗಳಂತೆ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಒಟ್ಟು ವಿರೋಧ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧ Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²).

narration.en: In series, the resistor voltage is in phase with the current while the reactive voltages are at 90°, so they add as vectors (phasors). The total opposition is the impedance Z = √R² + (XL - XC)² and I = V/Z. The phase angle is given by tan φ = (XL - XC)/R. If XL > XC the circuit is inductive (current lags); if XC > XL it is capacitive (current leads).
narration.kn: ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ರೋಧಕ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ಪ್ರವಾಹದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪ್ರತಿಘಾತ ವಿಭವಾಂತರಗಳು 90° ನಲ್ಲಿ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಅವು ಸದಿಶಗಳಂತೆ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಒಟ್ಟು ವಿರೋಧ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧ Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²).

say.en: In series, the resistor voltage is in phase with the current while the reactive voltages are at 90 degrees, so they add as vectors phasors. The total opposition is the impedance Z equals the square root of R squared plus (XL - XC) squared and I equals V over Z. The phase angle is given by tan phi equals (XL - XC)/R. If XL is greater than XC the circuit is inductive current lags; if XC is greater than XL it is capacitive current leads. RL: Z equals the square root of (R squared plus X L squared), current lags.
say.kn: ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ರೋಧಕ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ಪ್ರವಾಹದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪ್ರತಿಘಾತ ವಿಭವಾಂತರಗಳು 90 degrees ನಲ್ಲಿ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಅವು ಸದಿಶಗಳಂತೆ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಒಟ್ಟು ವಿರೋಧ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧ Z equals the square root of (R squared plus (XL - XC) squared).

say.en: RC: Z equals the square root of (R squared plus X C squared), current leads.
tan phi equals (X L - X C)/R.

title.en: On the board: Series RLC: impedance and phase

say.en: Here is R, L and C in series with an AC supply. The same current flows through all three.
Draw the phasors. VR is along the current. VL is 90 degrees ahead, pointing up, and VC is 90 degrees behind, pointing down.
VL and VC cancel partly. The supply voltage is the phasor sum of VR and VL minus VC, at angle phi.
Dividing every voltage by the current gives the impedance and the phase angle.
Example: R 30 ohms, XL 80 ohms and XC 40 ohms. The net reactance is 40, so Z is root of 30 squared plus 40 squared, 50 ohms.
The power factor is R over Z, 0.6, so phi is 53 degrees lagging. With 100 volts, I is 2 amperes and the true power is 120 watts.

body.en: Apparent power $S = VI$ is measured in volt-amperes (VA). True power, the power actually used, is $P = VI \cos φ$ in watts, and only the resistor consumes it: $P = I^2R$. Reactive power $Q = VI \sin φ$ is in VAR. The *power factor* is $\cos φ = R/Z$: 1 for a pure resistor and 0 for a pure L or C.
body.kn: ತೋರಿಕೆ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ S = VI (VA). ನಿಜ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P = VI cos φ (W), ಅದನ್ನು ರೋಧಕ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಅಂಶ cos φ = R/Z; ಶುದ್ಧ ರೋಧಕಕ್ಕೆ 1, ಶುದ್ಧ L ಅಥವಾ C ಗೆ 0.

narration.en: Apparent power S = VI is measured in volt-amperes (VA). True power, the power actually used, is P = VI cos φ in watts, and only the resistor consumes it: P = I²R. Reactive power Q = VI sin φ is in VAR. The power factor is cos φ = R/Z: 1 for a pure resistor and 0 for a pure L or C.
narration.kn: ತೋರಿಕೆ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ S = VI (VA). ನಿಜ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P = VI cos φ (W), ಅದನ್ನು ರೋಧಕ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಅಂಶ cos φ = R/Z; ಶುದ್ಧ ರೋಧಕಕ್ಕೆ 1, ಶುದ್ಧ L ಅಥವಾ C ಗೆ 0.

say.en: Apparent power S equals VI is measured in volt-amperes VA. True power, the power actually used, is P equals VI cos phi in watts, and only the resistor consumes it: P equals I squaredR. Reactive power Q equals VI sin phi is in VAR. The power factor is cos phi equals R over Z: 1 for a pure resistor and 0 for a pure L or C. S equals VI VA.
say.kn: ತೋರಿಕೆ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ S equals VI VA. ನಿಜ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P equals VI cos phi W, ಅದನ್ನು ರೋಧಕ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಅಂಶ cos phi equals R over Z; ಶುದ್ಧ ರೋಧಕಕ್ಕೆ 1, ಶುದ್ಧ L ಅಥವಾ C ಗೆ 0.

say.en: P equals VI cos phi equals I squaredR W.

tagline.en: R, L and C on AC, inductive and capacitive reactance, phase relations, impedance of series RL, RC and RLC circuits, and true power and power factor.

myth.en: The element voltages in a series AC circuit must add up to the supply voltage, so V_R = 184 V, V_L = 368 V and V_C = 230 V on a 230 V supply cannot be right.

truth.en: The voltages are out of phase and must be added as phasors: $V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$. A single element can even have more voltage than the supply. In DC circuits plain addition always works, so it feels like a law. In AC, V_L and V_C point in opposite directions on the phasor diagram and partly cancel, while V_R is at right angles to both.

say.en: X_L = 2πfL rises with frequency; X_C = 1/(2πfC) falls with frequency.
Pure L: I lags V by 90°; pure C: I leads V by 90°; neither uses average power.
Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²); I = V/Z.
Power factor cos φ = R/Z; true power P = VI cos φ = I²R.
Series AC voltages add as phasors, not as numbers.

goal.en: R, L and C on AC, inductive and capacitive reactance, phase relations, impedance of series RL, RC and RLC circuits, and true power and power factor.

task.en: Does the current lead, lag or stay in phase with the voltage?

explain.en: Net inductive circuits have lagging current, net capacitive circuits leading current, and a purely resistive (or resonant) circuit has the current in phase.

takeaway.en: X_L = 2πfL rises with frequency; X_C = 1/(2πfC) falls with frequency.

narration.en: Many people think: The element voltages in a series AC circuit must add up to the supply voltage, so V_R = 184 V, V_L = 368 V and V_C = 230 V on a 230 V supply cannot be right. Actually: The voltages are out of phase and must be added as phasors: $V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$. A single element can even have more voltage than the supply. In DC circuits plain addition always works, so it feels like a law. In AC, V_L and V_C point in opposite directions on the phasor diagram and partly cancel, while V_R is at right angles to both.

problem.en: A coil with R = 30 Ω and X_L = 40 Ω is connected to 100 V AC. Find Z, I, the power factor and the power.

answer.en: Z = 50 Ω, I = 2 A, pf 0.6 lagging, P = 120 W

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A coil with R = 30 Ω and X_L = 40 Ω is connected to 100 V AC. Find Z, I, the power factor and the power.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A coil with R equals 30 ohms and X L equals 40 ohms is connected to 100 volts AC. Find Z, I, the power factor and the power.
Z equals the square root of (30 squared plus 40 squared) equals the square root of 2500 equals 50 ohms.
I equals 100 over 50 equals 2 A; cos phi equals R over Z equals 30 over 50 equals 0.6 lagging.
P equals VI cos phi equals 100 times 2 times 0.6 equals 120 watts; check I squaredR equals 4 times 30 equals 120 watts.
So the answer is Z equals 50 ohms, I equals 2 A, pf 0.6 lagging, P equals 120 watts.

problem.en: A series RLC circuit has R = 8 Ω, X_L = 10 Ω and X_C = 4 Ω. Find Z, the phase angle and the nature of the circuit.

steps.en: tan φ = 6/8 = 0.75, φ = 36.9°; power factor = 0.8 lagging.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A series RLC circuit has R = 8 Ω, X_L = 10 Ω and X_C = 4 Ω. Find Z, the phase angle and the nature of the circuit.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A series RLC circuit has R equals 8 ohms, X L equals 10 ohms and X C equals 4 ohms. Find Z, the phase angle and the nature of the circuit.
Net reactance equals 10 minus 4 equals 6 ohms inductive.
Z equals the square root of 8 squared plus 6 squared equals the square root of 100 equals 10 ohms.
tan phi equals 6 over 8 equals 0.75, phi equals 36.9 degrees; power factor equals 0.8 lagging.
So the answer is Z equals 10 ohms, phi is approximately 36.9 degrees, inductive.

homework.en: A 60 Ω resistor and a capacitor with X_C = 80 Ω are in series across 200 V. Find I, the power factor and the power.

narration.en: Recap. Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and I = V/Z. X_L > X_C: inductive, current lags; X_C > X_L: capacitive, current leads. Power factor cos φ = R/Z; true power P = VI cos φ = I²R.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²), I = V/Z. XL > XC: ಪ್ರೇರಕ ಸ್ವಭಾವ, ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹಿಂದೆ; XC > XL: ಧಾರಕ ಸ್ವಭಾವ, ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಮುಂದೆ. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಅಂಶ cos φ = R/Z; ನಿಜ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P = VI cos φ = I²R.

answers.en: inductive, current lags; X_C > X_L: capacitive, current leads.
